problem_summary.summary: Return the number of words in the shortest one-letter-at-a-time transformation from beginWord to endWord, using dictionary words after the start, or 0 if impossible.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: beginWord, endWord, and a list of equal-length lowercase words. Return the shortest sequence length including both endpoints, or 0.
constraints: All words have the same length

brute_force.explanation: Build an explicit graph by comparing every pair of candidate words, connecting pairs with exactly one differing character. Then BFS from beginWord, counting the start as sequence length one.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Two words share an edge exactly when one legal transformation connects them. Paths correspond to valid transformation sequences, and BFS returns a path with the fewest edges; adding one converts edge count to number of words.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(N^2 L) to compare all word pairs, plus O(N^2) BFS in the explicit graph, where N is the number of dictionary words plus the start and L is word length.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(N^2) for the explicit adjacency lists and O(N) for BFS state.

optimized.explanation: Index each dictionary word under all wildcard patterns formed by replacing one position with '*'. BFS from beginWord looks up its patterns to find one-letter neighbors. Clear a pattern bucket after scanning it so it is not repeatedly traversed.
optimized.correctness_idea: Words in the same one-position wildcard bucket differ at most at that position; distinct words in the bucket are exactly one letter apart. Therefore bucket expansion exposes every legal next word. BFS preserves shortest sequence length, with the begin word counted as one.
optimized.time_complexity: O(N L^2) worst case for constructing and hashing N wildcard patterns of length L; each bucket is scanned at most once, with O(NL) total word references scanned.
optimized.space_complexity: O(NL^2) for wildcard pattern strings and bucket references, plus O(N) for BFS state.
